questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of policy-as-code and practical gate setup for Kubernetes manifests. It targets beginners learning to automate policy checks.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes securityContext
- Conftest and Rego
- CI integration for policy gates
- Manifest validation

## Code Example
```rego
package conftest.policy

# Deny hostNetwork/hostPID
deny[reason] {
  input.kind == "Pod"
  input.spec.hostNetwork == true
  reason = "hostNetwork must be disabled"
}
deny[reason] {
  input.kind == "Pod"
  input.spec.hostPID == true
  reason = "hostPID must be disabled"
}
# RunAsNonRoot checks for containers
deny[reason] {
  input.kind == "Pod"
  c := input.spec.containers[_]
  not c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  reason = "containers must set runAsNonRoot: true"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend the policy to cover initContainers?
- How would you lock down the policy version in CI to avoid silent regressions?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design progressive delivery gates at scale, with multi-cloud constraints and real-world SLO-based rollouts; focuses on policy, tooling (Argo Rollouts, Prometheus), and CI integration; evaluates trade-offs between safety and speed, failure modes; ensures observability and reproducibility.

## Key Concepts

- Progressive delivery with Argo Rollouts Canary
- AnalysisTemplate and Prometheus metrics
- Promotion rules based on consecutive analyses and SLO breach thresholds
- CI gates validating manifest shape and rollout strategy
- Rollback/promotion semantics in production

## Code Example

```yaml
# AnalysisTemplate (Prometheus-based)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-analysis
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: error-rate
    successCondition: result < 0.01
    failureCondition: result >= 0.05
    provider:
      prometheus:
        address: http://prometheus-operated.default.svc.cluster.local
        query: avg(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

```yaml
# Minimal Rollout using Canary
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myservice
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myservice
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myregistry/myservice:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-analysis
      stepWeight: 20
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test for promotion failure modes if the AnalysisTemplate temporarily becomes unavailable?
- How would you adapt this gate for multi-tenant environments with separate SLIs per tenant?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime, policy-driven security for multi-tenant clusters, including per-tenant exceptions, scalable policy storage, and practical CI validation.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego enforcement
- Runtime security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, hostPath, privileged, SETUID checks
- Central PolicyStore for per-tenant overrides
- CI validation: dry-run, Gatekeeper evaluation, and manifest validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: runtimepolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RuntimePolicy
        listKind: RuntimePolicyList
        plural: runtimepolicies
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package runtimepolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
        msg := "container must run as non-root"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        any_cont := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not any_cont.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "container must have readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      }
      # Additional rules for hostPath, privileged, and SETUID would follow similarly
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RuntimePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-runtime-policy
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    namespaces: ["tenant-a-*"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you manage updates to PolicyStore and revoke exceptions?
- How would you measure policy evaluation latency at scale?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical enforcement of runtime posture using admission controls and network egress in a multi-tenant data platform. Combines Gatekeeper and Kyverno with real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate with REGO to require envoy-proxy sidecar in confidential pods

- CI test plan with manifest validation; runtime validation via in-cluster policy, egress monitoring

## Code Example
```rego
package k8svalidation

deny["envoy-proxy sidecar required"] {
  input.review.object.metadata.labels["data-tier"] == "confidential"
  not has_sidecar(input.review.object.spec.containers, "envoy-proxy")
}

has_sidecar(containers, name) {
  containers[i].name == name
}
```

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: confidential-pod-security
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-envoy-sidecar
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          selector:
            matchLabels:
              data-tier: confidential
    validate:
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: envoy-proxy
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Why This Is Asked
Why this angle matters: binds image attestation, SBOM, secret management, and canary verification across clouds, aligning with production-grade trust.

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore cosign attestation
- SBOM requirements
- SecretStore-based injection
- Kyverno/OPA admission gates

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-sigstore-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: audit
  rules:
  - name: attest-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment, StatefulSet]
    validate:
      message: "image must be cosigned and SBOM present"
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/signature"]: "*"
        metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/sbom"]: "*"
```

```rego
# OPA policy (high level)
package gatekeeper
violation[{"msg": msg}]
default violation = []
violation = [{"msg": m} |
  input.request.kind == "Deployment" and
  not input.request.object.spec.template.metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/signature"]
  or not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/sbom"] ]
```

## Why This Is Asked

```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy (minimal)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secctx
```

questions.explanation:
## How It Works

Edge layers cache per-tenant state and call a central Redis-backed ledger via a Lua script that atomically consumes tokens. A regional coordinator ensures global quotas while keeping latency low. Time windows and heartbeat-based refresh bound drift. In Redis outage, fall back to in-process counters with strict backpressure and reconcile on recovery.

## Key Points

- **Atomicity**: Lua script executes in Redis to decrement tokens atomically.
- **Consistency**: cross-region quotas converge via central ledger with short TTL-based caches.
- **Failure handling**: circuit breaker, degraded mode with local counters, paced release when Redis returns.

## Example

```javascript
// Minimal working example
async function checkQuota(tenantId, tokens=1){
  const key = `quota:${tenantId}`;
  const now = Date.now();
  const lua = `
    local k = KEYS[1]
    local t = tonumber(ARGV[1])
    local rate = tonumber(ARGV[2])
    local cap = tonumber(ARGV[3])
    local need = tonumber(ARGV[4])
    local data = redis.call('hmget', k, 'tokens','last')
    local lol = tonumber(data[1] or cap)
    local last = tonumber(data[2] or now)
    local elapsed = math.max(0, now - last)
    lol = math.min(cap, lol + elapsed * rate / 1000)
    if lol >= need then
      lol = lol - need
      redis.call('hmset', k, 'tokens', lol, 'last', now)
      return lol
    else
      return -1
    end
  `
  const res = await redis.eval(lua, 1, key, now, rate, cap, tokens)
  return res
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic manifest linting and security checks in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes manifests
- YAML parsing with yq
- GitHub Actions gating
- SecurityContext and imagePullPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-manifest-gate.yml
name: Manifest Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate manifests
        run: |
          set -e
          violations=0
          for f in $(git diff --name-only origin/main | grep -E '\\.ya?ml$' ); do
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].readinessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].livenessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsNonRoot' "$f" | grep -q true; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsUser' "$f" | grep -q '1000'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].imagePullPolicy' "$f" | grep -q 'Always'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
          done
          if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing.yaml (no readiness/liveness probes or runAsNonRoot)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bad-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

```yaml
# passing.yaml (probes present, non-root, Always)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: good-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this gate to cover initContainers?

## Why This Question Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to integrate image provenance with runtime governance in a GPU-driven, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It spans CI pipelines, admission controls, and cross-system attestations—core skills for securing production ML platforms.

## Key Concepts
- **Image Provenance**: Using cosign and Rekor to cryptographically verify container image origins
- **SBOM Signing and Verification**: Ensuring software bills of materials are tamper-proof and traceable
- **Central Provenance Store**: A single source of truth for validated digest information
- **Admission Constraints**: Kyverno/OPA policies enforcing GPU type and quota at deploy time

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: Sign, generate SBOM, and attest
name: Gate: image provenance
on: [push]
env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
  SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.COSIGN_KEY }}

jobs:
  build-sign-attest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Generate and sign SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json=sbom.json
          cosign attest --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            --type sbom \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Upload to Rekor (automatic with cosign attest)
        run: |
          echo "Rekor entry created automatically during attestation"
      - name: Store central provenance digest
        run: |
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}')
          echo "${{ github.sha }}:$DIGEST" >> provenance_store.txt
```

```yaml
# Kyverno admission policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-gate
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-digest
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "ghcr.io/*"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/org/*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
          verifyDigest: true
          required: true
    - name: enforce-gpu-type
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      context:
        - name: namespace
          apiCall:
            urlPath: /api/v1/namespaces/{{ request.namespace }}
      preconditions:
        - key: "{{ request.namespace }}"
          operator: NotEquals
          value: "kube-system"
      validate:
        message: "GPU type must match namespace label"
        pattern:
          spec:
            template:
              spec:
                containers:
                  - (resources.limits."nvidia.com/gpu"): "?*"
    - name: enforce-gpu-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      validate:
        message: "GPU quota exceeded for namespace"
        deny: |
          {{ exists request.namespace.metadata.labels."gpu-quota" }}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of Kubernetes manifests is a practical, repeatable gate in real projects. This tests understanding of policy-as-code, tooling choices (Kyverno vs Gatekeeper), constraint design for host access controls and image source controls, and CI integration in GitHub Actions with ephemeral test clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper
- Constraints for host access (hostNetwork, hostPath, hostPort, privileged containers)
- Image source controls (allowed registries) and imagePullPolicy enforcement
- CI integration in GitHub Actions using KinD or similar ephemeral clusters

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-host-access
spec:
  rules:
  - name: block-host-network
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork is not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
  - name: block-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not allowed"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ contains(element.volumes[].hostPath, '') }}"
          operator: "NotEqual"
          value: ""
```

## Minimal Policy (Combined)
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: security-guardrails
spec:
  rules:
  - name: deny-host-network-port
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork and hostPort are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
          hostPort: "0"
  - name: deny-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not permitted"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ @ }}"
          operator: "AnyNotIn"
          value: [""]
      foreach:
        - list: "spec.volumes[?hostPath]"
          deny: true
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Privileged containers are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              privileged: "false"
  - name: allowed-registries
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Images must come from approved registries"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "registry.company.com/*"
            imagePullPolicy: "Always"
```

## Failing Manifest (hostPath + hostNetwork)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: docker.io/myapp:latest
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: host-volume
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: host-volume
    hostPath:
      path: /etc
```

## Passing Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.company.com/myapp:v1.0
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Validation
```bash
# Install Kyverno locally
brew install kyverno

# Apply policies
kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml

# Validate a manifest
kyverno validate insecure-pod.yaml
```

## CI Validation (GitHub Actions)
```yaml
name: Validate Manifests
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Create KinD cluster
      run: kind create cluster
    - name: Install Kyverno
      run: |
        kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/releases/latest/download/install.yaml
        kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app=kyverno -n kyverno --timeout=120s
    - name: Apply policies
      run: kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f insecure-pod.yaml || echo "Expected failure"
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f secure-pod.yaml
```

## Why This Is Asked

Assess mastery of reproducible builds, attestation, SBOMs, and supply chain controls in CI/CD for a multi-service repo.

## Key Concepts

- Reproducible builds, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
- Image signing with cosign and attestation
- SBOM generation with Syft and verification against digest
- Monorepo with multiple languages and per-service artifacts

## Code Example

```yaml
name: Repro Build Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build deterministically
        run: |
          export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct HEAD)
          docker buildx build --build-arg SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --tag $IMAGE .
      - name: Sign image
        run: cosign sign $IMAGE
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: syft packages docker://${IMAGE} -o spdx
      - name: Verify
        run: cosign verify --signature public.key --certificate-identity-id "monorepo" $IMAGE
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate cosign keys and SBOM verification keys?
- How do you handle caching and parallelization in a large mono-repo?

```javascript
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-restricted-ps
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce

    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Namespace"]
    validate:
      message: "Namespace must declare restricted PS via label"
      pattern:
        metadata:

  - name: auto-label-namespace
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Namespace"]
    mutate:
      patchStrategicMerge:

```
